CDC analyzed self-reported data from the 2012 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) survey
Data from all 50 states and the District of Columbia were included.

methods_quotes.q: The 2012 BRFSS data were weighted using the raking method
Annual rates of alcohol-impaired driving episodes were calculated by dividing the annual number of episodes by the respective weighted population estimate
For the 13 respondents who reported more than one episode daily, annualized alcohol-impaired driving episodes were truncated at 360.
Rates were suppressed for five states because the number of episodes was <50 or the standard error was >30%.
Differences between subgroups were analyzed using t-tests, with a p value of ≤0.05 indicating statistical significance.
